A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AVA-Bench and contain readable main text and Appendices A-D. Corresponding figures, tables, equations and results support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of nine vision foundation models across 14 atomic visual abilities, including Table 4, bounding-box ablations and subgroup analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and analyses in Sections 4-6 and Appendix C, including the detailed results in Table 4.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and evaluation procedure are unchanged: LLaVA-style preparation followed by per-ability connector and LLM LoRA tuning while keeping the vision model frozen.

E1.justification: Sections 3 and Appendix A retain the same 14 abilities, 26 source datasets and represented domains. The evaluated scenarios, including spatial reasoning with and without bounding boxes, are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 4 and corresponding comparisons retain SigLIP-1/2, AIMv2, CLIP, InternVL-2.5, RADIOv2.1, DINOv2, SAM and MiDas-3.0. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The data splits, filtering, sample counts, metrics and Table 3 training settings remain unchanged. Both versions also retain the same comparison of Qwen2 0.5B and Vicuna-1.5 7B evaluators.

E4.justification: Both retain the bounding-box ablation in Figure 9, localization-size analysis in Figure 10, connector probing in Section 6 and subgroup analyses in Appendix C.2. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain the fixed-seed sampling statements in Appendix A.2. Neither reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests, and uncertainty reporting does not change.

E6.justification: Table 4 values and rankings are identical, including SigLIP-2 OCR ANLS of 81.18 and DINOv2 orientation accuracy of 85.54. The plotted results, connector-probing values and qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The ability definitions and metric equations in Appendix B.1 are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: Both retain the same claims about disentangling 14 abilities, diagnosing model strengths and preserving rankings with a 0.5B evaluator at approximately eightfold lower cost. The open-source release claim also remains.

C2.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C.2 retain the same interpretations concerning language alignment, representation convergence, object-size effects and long-text OCR limitations. Added citations do not introduce new explanations or qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 removes the first-page project URL, with no replacement project or code link elsewhere, while retaining the code-release claim. This reduces access information; the PDFs do not establish any change in actual resource availability. Technical disclosures otherwise match.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 110 to 118 works without removing existing references. Additions concern specialized MLLMs, video alignment, SAM and five continual-learning works; Appendix D.2 now cites the latter around 'continual development.' The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 removes Jihyung Kil and the Adobe Research affiliation from the author block, makes small wording and citation edits, and introduces an empty citation marker in Appendix C.2. Section order and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shorter first-page header shifts Figure 1 and the abstract upward, and additional references reflow the bibliography. The 30 figures and four tables retain their content, design, numbering and section placement.

improvement.justification: Added references modestly expand context, while scientific evidence and explanations remain unchanged. Removing the sole project URL despite retaining the code-release claim reduces resource discoverability, and Appendix C.2 gains an empty citation marker. These produce a limited decline in usability and editorial quality.
